q: Which comorbidity should be looked for behind an abscess?
o: Diabetes, sepsis or IV drug use

q: Which feature suggests necrotising fasciitis over cellulitis?
o: Pain out of proportion to examination

q: What type of necrotising fasciitis is polymicrobial and perineal?
why: Type 2 is group A strep; type 3 is Vibrio.

q: Which antibiotic is added for its anti-toxin effect in necrotising fasciitis or TSS?
why: Follow local guidelines; inhibits toxin production.

q: What is the intraoperative finding of necrotising fasciitis?
o: Lack of resistance to blunt dissection and dishwater pus

q: How does toxic shock syndrome cause shock?
o: A superantigen activating many T-cells, causing cytokine storm

q: What is the DKA insulin regimen?
o: Fixed-rate IV insulin 0.1 units/kg/h, continuing long-acting insulin

q: What is the target rate of ketone fall in DKA?
What happens to an insulin pump perioperatively if glucose rises above about 12?
o: Stop the pump and switch to IV insulin
